overall_summary: Deduplication of 47 unique videos reveals a clear performance divergence: first-person visceral hypothetical hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic/geological extremes generate top-tier reach (800-1,050+ views, 3-4% like rate), whereas abstract psychology factoids ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and duplicate posts suffer severe audience drop-off (<60 views, near-zero engagement). Videos formatted between 19 and 21 seconds consistently out-engage shorter sub-16-second clips by delivering structured narrative tension rather than isolated trivia.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Experiential Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dramatically outperformed third-person declarative titles.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme science, mystery, and astronomical hazards as immediate, sensory first-person simulations rather than passive encyclopedia facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Top performers ('Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' at 981 views, TrES-2b at 1,029 views, liquid diamond planet at 1,029 views) are all 19-21s, allowing for setup, escalating peril, and a punchy cognitive twist.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize production at 19-21 seconds to maintain the 3-beat structure: Visceral Hook (0-3s) -> Sensory Escalation (4-14s) -> Counter-intuitive Climax (15-20s).

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract Internal Psychology / Intangible Mental Concepts
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was reposted three times across September with stagnant totals (5, 10, and 53 views; 0 likes); 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' generated only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Retire ungrounded cognitive/memory factoids unless anchored to a high-stakes visual survival or tangible physical manifestation.

weak_patterns.pattern: Direct Topic Duplication Without Hook Mutation
weak_patterns.evidence: Posting identical titles ('Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted on Sep 11 and Sep 23; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' posted 3 times) fragmented algorithm test impressions and suppressed CTR.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication; never re-upload unchanged angles or verbatim titles.
